title: Signed first-quadrant Hom model for a module target
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $M^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $u\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $M^a=0$ for $a>u$, and let $N$ be an $A$-module. Then there exists an injective resolution $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] with $I^i=0$ for $i<0$. For every such resolution, the following data define a commuting first-quadrant double complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] in $A$-modules:
$$D^{i,b}=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^{u-b},I^i)\quad(i,b\geq0),\qquad D^{i,b}=0\quad\text{otherwise},$$
$$d_\mathrm{I}(f)=d_I^i\circ f,\qquad d_\mathrm{II}(f)=(-1)^{b-u+1}f\circ d_M^{u-b-1}.$$
Put $T^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ with the product terms and differential $d_T(f)=d_If-(-1)^t f d_M$ in degree $t$ [def-pur-hom-complex], interpreted on the one-object identity-covering ringed site with coefficient ring $A$. Let $Q^t=\operatorname{Tot}(D)^{t+u}$ with $d_Q^t=d_{\operatorname{Tot}(D)}^{t+u}$; this specifies degree translation with unchanged differential, independently of signed-shift conventions. The finite-coordinate reindexing $a=u-b$, $i=a+t$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism of complexes $T^\bullet\cong Q^\bullet$. In the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ it induces an isomorphism
$$Q^\bullet\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^\bullet,N[0]),$$
where derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on that same ringed site. No boundedness below, projectivity or finite-generation assumption on $M^\bullet$, and no Noetherian assumption on $A$, is required.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives], the category of $A$-modules is abelian and has enough injectives. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] to the object $N$ in this category (with the auxiliary abelian category also chosen to be $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$). It gives an injective resolution $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ with $I^i=0$ for $i<0$. This proves the existence assertion. Fix any such resolution for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (1); module-category hypothesis: more-algebra.tex Tag 01DD, lemma-injectives-modules

proof.text: Define $D$ and its two differentials by the formulas in the statement, with all maps involving a zero term outside the quadrant equal to zero. Composition is $A$-linear because $A$ is commutative. We have $d_{\mathrm I}^2(f)=d_I^{i+1}d_I^i f=0$ and $d_{\mathrm{II}}^2(f)=(-1)^{b-u+1}(-1)^{b-u+2}f d_M^{u-b-1}d_M^{u-b-2}=0$. The two mixed composites both send $f\in D^{i,b}$ to $(-1)^{b-u+1}d_I^i f d_M^{u-b-1}$: increasing $i$ does not change the sign of $d_{\mathrm{II}}$. The same identities hold at the boundary since the missing terms are zero. Thus these are commuting differentials and $D$ is a first-quadrant double complex in precisely the convention of [def-sp-double-complex-total].

source.place: Tag 0FNB, section-double-complexes, definition-double-complex; explicit verification for this signed Hom family

proof.text: Write $T^t=\prod_{a\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^a,I^{a+t})$ using [def-pur-hom-complex]. A factor is zero for $a>u$ because its source is zero, and for $a<-t$ because its target is zero. Hence only the finite interval $-t\leq a\leq u$ can contribute. Set $i=a+t$ and $b=u-a$; this bijects that interval with the pairs $i,b\geq0$, $i+b=t+u$. Define $\phi^t:T^t\to Q^t$ by placing $f^a$ in the summand $(a+t,u-a)$ of the finite direct sum in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Its inverse assigns that coordinate to $f^a$ for $-t\leq a\leq u$ and the unique zero map to every other factor. These maps are $A$-linear and inverse coordinatewise. If $t+u<0$, both the interval and the diagonal are empty, and this is the unique isomorphism between zero modules.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes, product formula; homology.tex Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex, finite direct-sum formula

proof.text: Check the differentials on a coordinate $f^a:M^a\to I^i$, where $i=a+t$, $b=u-a$. The $d_{\mathrm I}$ contribution of the total differential is $d_I^i f^a$ in position $(i+1,b)$, corresponding to source degree $a$ in $T^{t+1}$. The $d_{\mathrm{II}}$ contribution lies in position $(i,b+1)$, corresponding to source degree $a-1$, and equals $(-1)^i(-1)^{b-u+1}f^a d_M^{a-1}=(-1)^{t+1}f^a d_M^{a-1}$, since $i+b-u=t$. Combining the incoming contributions at source degree $a$, the inverse coordinate map therefore gives $d_I^{a+t}f^a+(-1)^{t+1}f^{a+1}d_M^a$, exactly $(d_Tf)^a$ by [def-pur-hom-complex]. Coordinates outside the interval are zero on both sides. Thus $d_Q^t\phi^t=\phi^{t+1}d_T^t$, using the total sign in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. As $Q$ uses the unchanged differential, no extra shift sign occurs. The coordinatewise inverse also commutes with the differentials by this equality, proving the asserted isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex; more-algebra.tex Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes, differential sign rule

proof.text: The chosen $I^\bullet$ is bounded below and each $I^i$ is injective, so [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] makes it K-injective. On the one-object category with only the identity morphism and identity covering, a sheaf of modules over $A$ is just an $A$-module: there is one module to specify, identity restriction, and no additional sheaf condition; sheaf Hom and its product complex are the ordinary module Hom and the product complex $T$. Consequently [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], including its assertion for any K-injective representative of the target, identifies $T$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^\bullet,N[0])$ in $D(A)$. Apply the localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to the complex isomorphism $\phi:T\cong Q$ and compose its inverse with this identification. This gives $Q\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M^\bullet,N[0])$. Only the upper bound on $M$ and nonnegative injective terms of $I$ were used; the source modules need no projectivity or finite generation, and the ring need not be Noetherian.
